pages.text: $(italic)$(#6b5a45)Put the file in your datapack under $(#8a5a2b)data/<namespace>/element_mappings/$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) and $(#8a5a2b)/reload$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) picks it up. $(bold)The file name means nothing here$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) — what prices anything is the $(#8a5a2b)block$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45), $(#8a5a2b)item$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) and $(#8a5a2b)build_cost$()$(italic)$(#6b5a45) written inside it.$()$(br2)The element mappings are the single ledger of what a thing is worth in elements. What the Crafting Station charges to make it, what the workstation yields for taking it apart, what a shop sells it for, what finding one in a chest is worth, and even whether it counts as a material at all — every one of those reads this table.

$(bold)Key  Meaning$()$(li)block — prices a block, by block registry id$(li)item — prices an item, by item registry id$(li)build_cost — a map from element to a whole number, keyed by one of the seven elements$(li)disabled — a boolean that takes it out of the element economy
pages.title: Fields

pages.text: One of $(#8a5a2b)block$() or $(#8a5a2b)item$() is enough; a file with neither means nothing. Write it as a block and the block's item form is priced along with it; write only $(#8a5a2b)item$() and a block lookup will not find it.
pages.title: block and item

pages.text: $(#8a5a2b)build_cost$() is an item's $(bold)canonical value$(), not what it costs to place. Several things charge against it: a workstation synthesis task spends it; taking an item apart in the workstation yields the value divided by the decompose divisor, which the Settings Center can adjust; a shop sells it with the shop's profit on top; an exploration chest prices its whole loot table through it; and the scanner values a patch of ground with it.
pages.title: Who Reads the Value

pages.text: Buildings and roads only request $(bold)mapped$() blocks from the warehouse. A block with no mapping is never requested at all — so a single mistyped item id produces no error whatsoever, it just quietly makes that block free material that builds anyway. This is the easiest place in the table to lose money.
pages.title: No Mapping Means Free

pages.text: $(#8a5a2b)disabled$() is not merely "sits out the economy": any building or road containing that block is $(bold)refused placement outright$(), a deliberate rule that a banned block must never turn into free material. The $(#8a5a2b)disabled/$() subfolder in the mod's own data means nothing at all — the scan is recursive and files inside it load like any other. The field is the only switch.
pages.title: disabled Has Teeth

pages.text: To change a price the mod already has, your file must sit in the $(bold)$(#8a5a2b)wandscape$()$(bold) namespace under the same file name$(), overriding it by datapack priority. A different file name does not work: the registry key is the file name with the namespace stripped, the mod's own copy wins a collision and yours is dropped whole, and even if both survived, a lookup returns whichever comes first in hash order, so which one wins is not defined.
pages.title: Overriding the Mod's Own Mappings

pages.text: One bad element key, such as $(#8a5a2b)matel$() for $(#8a5a2b)metal$(), makes the whole file fail to parse and be discarded, with a warning in the log. That is the only mistake in here that makes a noise.
pages.title: The Cost of One Bad Key

pages.text: The mod also ships $(#8a5a2b)element_seeds.json$(), a hand-written baseline price list of some four hundred entries. It is $(bold)only$() an input to one developer command: it prices nothing at runtime and no datapack can override it.
pages.title: Element Seeds

pages.text: $(#8a5a2b)/wandscape test generate_element_mappings$() takes the seeds as a baseline and works backwards through vanilla recipes to produce a whole batch of mapping files; $(#8a5a2b)--dry-run$() shows the plan first and $(#8a5a2b)--force$() overwrites hand-written files that already exist.$(br2)Note that it writes into a $(bold)developer's source tree$() — it is for editing the mod's own data on your own machine, and should not be run on a server.
pages.title: The Generator Command
